purpose: Store mathematical representations as reusable instructional tools linked to concepts, pedagogical purposes, evidence and system-specific usage. A representation must not be treated as exclusive to a country or curriculum.

representations.name_cn: 数的组成 / 部分—部分—整体
representations.mathematical_structure: A whole can be decomposed into parts and recomposed; addition and subtraction describe inverse relationships among the same quantities.
teacher_moves: Ask pupils to find more than one decomposition of the same whole.
Keep the whole constant while varying the parts.
Connect the diagram to equations in more than one orientation.
Ask what is known, what is unknown and what relationship stays unchanged.
common_misuses: Treating the diagram as a decorative template rather than discussing the relationship between parts and whole.
Only using it for addition and failing to connect subtraction/inverse relationships.

representations.mathematical_structure: Quantities are organised relative to five and ten, helping pupils see composition, complements and subitising patterns without recounting every item.
teacher_moves: Ask how many are seen without counting one-by-one.
Ask how many more are needed to make ten.
Show the same number in different arrangements and compare what is easier to see.
Connect filled and empty spaces to equations.
common_misuses: Using random placements that obscure the five-and-ten structure.
Keeping pupils dependent on the frame after facts should be recalled fluently.

representations.name_cn: 十进制位值材料 / 位值积木
representations.mathematical_structure: Units are nested by powers of ten; regrouping is exchanging equivalent quantities across adjacent place-value units.
teacher_moves: Name the unit represented by each piece rather than relying only on size.
Physically exchange ten of one unit for one of the next unit.
Place materials beside written notation so each regrouping step has a structural meaning.
Change the designated whole when moving into decimals so pupils do not overgeneralise object size.
common_misuses: Teaching carrying/borrowing language without linking it to unit exchange.
Assuming a physical piece always has a fixed numerical value independent of the defined whole.

representations.mathematical_structure: Numbers are positions on a continuous ordered line; distance, direction, magnitude and interval can be represented spatially.
teacher_moves: Distinguish a number as a point from an interval as a length.
Use both labelled and partially labelled lines.
Ask pupils to justify relative position rather than only locate known marks.
Connect jumps to additive or multiplicative relationships without turning every calculation into repeated counting.
common_misuses: Treating fractions only as shaded parts of shapes and not as numbers with positions.
Counting tick marks instead of intervals.
Using number-line jumps mechanically without discussing magnitude or structure.

representations.mathematical_structure: Equal rows and columns expose multiplicative structure, commutativity, factors and decomposition of products.
teacher_moves: Ask what each dimension represents and distinguish number of groups from group size.
Rotate an array to discuss commutativity while preserving the quantities represented.
Partition an array to expose distributivity.
Connect the same array to multiplication and division equations.
common_misuses: Reducing arrays to pictures for memorising facts instead of reasoning about structure.
Using repeated addition as the only interpretation of multiplication.

representations.name_cn: 条形模型 / 线段模型
representations.mathematical_structure: Relative lengths encode quantitative relationships among knowns, unknowns, parts and wholes so that the problem structure can be separated from surface context.
teacher_moves: Build from the situation before drawing the bars.
Ask what each bar or section represents and whether lengths should be equal or unequal.
Hide or vary the unknown position so pupils reason from structure rather than keywords.
Connect the completed model to an equation.
common_misuses: Teaching bar models as a fixed problem-solving procedure.
Drawing bars without preserving quantitative relationships.
Using the representation after an equation is already obvious, adding cognitive load rather than clarity.

representations.name_cn: 面积模型 / 矩形模型
representations.mathematical_structure: A product is represented as the area of a rectangle, making factor decomposition and the distributive property visible.
teacher_moves: Label dimensions and connect each partial region to a partial product.
Partition factors by place value and recombine partial products.
Use the same rectangular structure to connect whole-number and fraction multiplication where mathematically appropriate.
Move progressively from drawn regions to symbolic distributive notation.
common_misuses: Treating boxes as an algorithm without connecting dimensions to factors.
Allowing an area-model procedure to become a permanent substitute for efficient fluent calculation.

representations.mathematical_structure: Factors are decomposed by place value and multiplication is distributed across the decomposed parts before products are recombined.
teacher_moves: Connect each partial product to place-value units and, where useful, an array or area model.
Compare expanded recording with the compact standard algorithm.
Ask which quantities are implicit in compact notation.
Fade the expanded form when pupils can maintain the place-value structure mentally.
common_misuses: Treating partial products and the standard algorithm as unrelated methods.
Retaining expanded recording after it stops supporting understanding or accuracy.

representations.mathematical_structure: Compact symbolic procedures encode place-value decomposition, unit exchange and operation properties efficiently.
teacher_moves: Explain the place-value meaning of each recorded step before expecting fluent use.
Compare compact notation with an earlier representation when diagnosing misconceptions.
Use estimation or inverse operations to check reasonableness.
Once secure, prioritise efficient and accurate execution rather than requiring a concrete representation for every calculation.
common_misuses: Teaching digit manipulation as an unexplained rule.
Requiring multiple representations indefinitely after the algorithm is understood and fluent.
Treating conceptual understanding and procedural fluency as competing goals.
